messages.content:
You answer a question about machinery and work-equipment law using ONLY the numbered passages given.

Rules:
- Use only these passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- If the passages do not answer the question, the kind is "unknown" and the value is null.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with the dates in the passages.
- If the question asks "which" or "what" and several passages answer it, list every one of them.
- If the question asks who does something and within what time, the kind is "text" and the value names both.
- Return JSON only:
  {"kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the article or annex point",
   "used": [passage numbers you relied on]}

Today is 2026-11-14.
Question: On 16 January 2027, can machinery conforming to Directive 2006/42/EC still be placed on the market?

Passages:
[0] REG, Art. 52(1): Article 52 Transitional provisions. 1. Member States shall not impede the making available on the market of products which were placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 14 January 2027. However, Chapter VI of this Regulation shall apply, from 13 July 2023, mutatis mutandis to such products instead of Article 11 of that Directive, including products for which a procedure has already been initiated under Article 11 of Directive 2006/42/EC.

[1] eu-dir-2014-35, Art. 25: Article 25 Transitional provisions Member States shall not impede the making available on the market of electrical equipment covered by Directive 2006/95/EC which is in conformity with that Directive and which was placed on the market before 20 April 2016.

[2] DIR, Art. 27: Article 27 Derogation Until 29 June 2011 Member States may allow the placing on the market and the putting into service of portable cartridge-operated fixing and other impact machinery which are in conformity with the national provisions in force upon adoption of this Directive.

[3] REG, Recital 1: (1) Directive 2006/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 3 ) was adopted in the context of establishing the internal market, in order to harmonise health and safety requirements for machinery in all Member States and to remove obstacles to trade in machinery between Member States.

[4] DIR, Recital 6: (6) It is appropriate to exclude from the scope of this Directive weapons, including firearms, that are subject to Council Directive 91/477/EEC of 18 June 1991 on control of the acquisition and possession of weapons ( 6 ) ; the exclusion of firearms should not apply to portable cartridge-operated fixing and other impact machinery designed for industrial or technical purposes only. It is necessary to provide for transitional arrangements enabling Member States to authorise the placing on the market and putting into service of such machinery manufactured in accordance with national provisions in force upon adoption of this Directive, including those implementing the Convention of 1 July 1969 on the Reciprocal Recognition of Proofmarks on Small Arms. Such transitional arrangements will also enable the European standardisation organisations to draft standards ensuring the safety level based on the state of the art.

[5] eu-dir-2014-68, Art. 48(2): Article 48 Transitional provisions. 2. Member States shall not impede the making available on the market and/or the putting into service of pressure equipment or assemblies covered by Directive 97/23/EC which are in conformity with that Directive and which were placed on the market before 1 June 2015.

[6] REG, Art. 51(2): Article 51 Repeals. 2. Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from 14 January 2027. References to the repealed Directive 2006/42/EC shall be construed as references to this Regulation and shall be read in accordance with the correlation table in Annex XII.

[7] eu-dir-2014-35, Recital 36: (36) It is necessary to provide for reasonable transitional arrangements that allow the making available on the market, without the need to comply with further product requirements, of electrical equipment which has already been placed on the market in accordance with Directive 2006/95/EC before the date of application of national measures transposing this Directive. Distributors should therefore be able to supply electrical equipment that has been placed on the market, namely stock that is already in the distribution chain, before the date of application of national measures transposing this Directive.

[8] eu-reg-2016-425, Art. 47(1): Article 47 Transitional provisions. 1. Without prejudice to paragraph 2, Member States shall not impede the making available on the market of products covered by Directive 89/686/EEC which are in conformity with that Directive and which were placed on the market before 21 April 2019.

[9] eu-dir-2014-30, Art. 43: Article 43 Transitional provisions Member States shall not impede the making available on the market and/or the putting into service of equipment covered by Directive 2004/108/EC which is in conformity with that Directive and which was placed on the market before 20 April 2016.

response.text: {"kind": "boolean", "value": false, "text": "No. Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from 14 January 2027 (Art. 51(2) of the Regulation). The transitional rule in Art. 52(1) protects only products placed on the market in conformity with that Directive before 14 January 2027, so it does not cover new placing on 16 January 2027. The passages do not expressly say that new placing is prohibited, only that the protection is limited to products placed before that date.", "used": [0, 6]}
